Turkey’s Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency’s decision to revoke  the bank’s main Istanbul branch’s licence after 44 years did not directly link the move to US sanctions, Al Jazeera reported. Washington designated the bank in 2018, accusing it of providing financial support to Mehr Eqtesad Bank, which the US links to Iran’s Basij.

items.summary: Iranian arms and advice helped Yemen's Houthis seize key Red Sea city, sources say The lightning Houthi advance down Yemen's Red Sea coast this week came with direct guidance from Iran's Revolutionary Guards seeking to open a new front in US-Israeli war on Iran, according to Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources. Iran told the Houthis last week to escalate their attacks on Saudi Arabia, a close US ally, and promised more funding, weapons and senior officers to help them do so, two Iranian sources said. Several senior Revolutionary Guards commanders had already travelled to Yemen to oversee and command Houthi attacks directed against Saudi Arabia after weeks of discussions over military strategy, a regional diplomat briefed by Tehran said. A third Iranian source, an official, said Iran had held several meetings with allies including the Houthis and that the move on Mocha was a Houthi rather than Iranian decision. However, it had helped Iran by putting upward pressure on oil prices and hurting the United States and Saudi Arabia, the official added. Reporting by Reuters

Malki described the incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca, following what the coalition said was a ballistic missile launch in July 2017. items.summary: Saudi Arabian pipeline outage threatens global oil supply Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4 percent of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders told Reuters on Sunday. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs since the start of the US-Iran war. Following the drone attacks launched from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to shut its huge East-West oil pipeline on Friday, Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay offline. Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing.

Macron said the meeting would focus on coordinating strategic stockpile levels, cooperation on exports and production capacity, and possible releases of strategic reserves. Macron said that the aim of the meeting was to strengthen cooperation and avoid unnecessary tensions between G7 countries and their key partners. He said France had initiated an international defence mission with the International Maritime Organization last April aimed at escorting tankers and container ships through the strategic waterway once an agreement was reached. Macron said reopening Hormuz depended on a deal between Iran and the United States, which he said appeared unlikely in the short term. items.summary: US opposes Iran nuclear chief attending IAEA conference The United States opposed the head of Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation attending the annual conference of the UN nuclear watchdog, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Monday. Speaking to reporters in Vienna, where the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is based, Wright said Mohammad Eslami was subject to US sanctions and had been denied a request for a waiver. “He’s a sanctioned individual and we don’t want sanctioned individuals evading their sanctions. He asked for a waiver of the sanctions and it was denied,” Wright said. Eslami has regularly attended and addressed the IAEA General Conference since becoming head of Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation in 2021. Iranian state television said Eslami and a delegation travelled to Vienna on a regular flight Saturday but were “blocked on the way because of obstructions by the United States”.

items.title: Houthi attacks expose gaps in Pakistan's defence pact with Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Houthi attacks expose gaps in Pakistan's defence pact with Saudi Arabia After positioning itself as a regional mediator by facilitating talks between Washington and Tehran, Pakistan marked a major milestone in its expanding diplomacy last month: the signing of a trilateral defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in Islam’s holiest city. Signed in Mecca on 7 August, the Joint Defence Agreement states that an attack on one signatory will be treated as an attack on all, drawing immediate comparisons to Nato’s Article 5, even as analysts cautioned against taking the clause too literally. That commitment was quickly tested on 8 September, when Iran-backed Houthi forces launched a massive drone and missile barrage into Saudi Arabia, striking critical military and energy infrastructure. Overnight, an abstract commitment turned into a high-stakes operational question. Neither Islamabad nor Ankara launched military counter-operations alongside Riyadh, choosing firm diplomatic statements instead. items.title: Pakistan ready to implement Mecca pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, defence minister says
items.summary: Pakistan ready to implement Mecca pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, defence minister says Pakistan has said it is ready to implement its defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, amid recent Houthi attacks. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said in an interview with Pakistani TV channel Geo News that the Mecca agreement - a defence deal between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey - "applies to us and we will fulfil our duty". He affirmed that Islamabad remains committed to protecting Saudi Arabia and its holy sites. Asif added that there was "absolutely no ambiguity" about the implementation of the defence pact, but did not disclose any further details about its defence strategy. He further said that Pakistan had conveyed Saudi Arabia's message to Iran over the Houthi attacks, and insisted that Iran would not "open another front".

Brent crude for November delivery gained 2.8 percent to $107.54 a barrel, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate for October rose 2.3 percent to $102.34. clusters.headline: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports

items.title: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports
items.summary: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports Top White House advisers, including vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio, have privately warned president Donald Trump that the conflict with Iran could extend through the remainder of his presidency, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials. The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The advisers told Trump in private discussions in the Oval Office and the Situation Room that Tehran could continue to resist US pressure, potentially prolonging the conflict beyond Inauguration Day in January 2029, the Journal added. The reported warning contrasts with Trump's own public remarks about the war. The president said on Wednesday he expected the war to end "immediately after" the US midterm elections in November, arguing that Iran was trying to influence the vote but would be unable to sustain its resistance much longer. Trump also acknowledged diplomatic talks are still a possibility but were not preferred. Report by Reuters

items.summary: An estimated 125,000 people, including more than 57,000 children, have fled since hostilities erupted in July between the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, the Yemeni government and its ally Saudi Arabia, with the UN calling it one of the most rapid and volatile waves of displacement in Yemen in years. items.title: The Houthis could tip the Iran war in Tehran's favor
items.summary: The conflict between the United States and Iran has become a contest in enduring economic pain and the political consequences that may flow from that pain. This has characterized the conflict since the breakdown of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in June that had raised brief hopes that the war would end. Each side appears confident that it can outlast the other in the pain-endurance contest. Fundamental change of this situation is unlikely anytime soon despite some indications Iran is considering military escalation as a possible way to break the stalemate. The Trump administration, after the failure of other options, appears to be hoping that the Iranian regime either will be toppled by an economically strained Iranian public or will somehow give up and make concessions. One of the more significant recent developments with potential for changing this stalemate, however, is renewed military action by the Houthi regime in Yemen, which includes interdicting shipping traversing the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait. items.title: Over 150 countries reject US decision to bar Palestinian delegation from upcoming UN General Assembly
items.summary: Over 150 countries reject US decision to bar Palestinian delegation from upcoming UN General Assembly On Thursday, 152 countries voted in favour of a resolution adopted by the UN General Assembly, rejecting the US's decision to prevent the Palestinian delegation from participating in the upcoming UN General Assembly session in New York City. The resolution called on Washington to reverse the decision, considering it a clear violation of the Headquarters Agreement, which legally obliges the host country to facilitate the entry of diplomatic delegations. The US State Department said on Thursday it has greenlit visas for a core Iranian delegation and essential staffers to take part in the meeting, but denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian officials visas.

US spokesperson Anna Kelly said the UN’s Human Rights Council has “accomplished nothing for human rights while spouting unserious nonsense for decades”, according to remarks carried by The Washington Post on Thursday. “The only party in this conflict that has committed war crimes is the Iranian regime,” Kelly added.

items.title: «Les deux vies et trois morts» du réalisateur iranien Karim Lakzadeh
items.summary: C'est une fable acerbe de l’Iran aujourd’hui, macabre et burlesque, avec un équilibre parfait entre l’humour noir et une critique sociale féroce. Dans le film Living Twice, Dying Thrice (« Deux vies, trois morts »), Karim Lakzadeh, né en 1986 à Chiraz, dans la province du Fars en Iran, raconte l’histoire de trois mineurs qui traversent le pays clandestinement. Victimes de l’effondrement d’une mine, ils décident de se faire déclarer morts pour commencer une deuxième vie. Présenté en première mondiale au Festival de Cannes, le film sera projeté au cinéma Louxor, à Paris, à l’occasion de la reprise de la programmation de l’ACID, du 17 au 20 septembre, dédiée au renouvellement des regards cinématographiques.

items.summary: The extraordinary success of the rebels, and Saudi counterstrikes, threaten economic havoc. But the country’s civilians are paying the highest price Even in a region beset by turmoil and learning to expect the unexpected, the lightning advance of Yemen’s Houthis along the Red Sea coast has shocked observers. More than 100,000 people have been forced to flee in a country where immiseration and displacement have become routine and half the population depend on humanitarian aid. The Iran war has forced Saudi Arabia to rely on moving oil via its east-west pipeline to Red Sea ports. items.title: Trump's govt makes 'treasonous' claim of weapons shortages
items.summary: In the last two days, a pair of government reports confirmed what many outside analysts have claimed: the Iran war has been extraordinarily costly for the U.S. military and for the American public. A Congressional Budget Office (CBO) analysis released Tuesday afternoon found that the Iran war has already cost the Department of Defense (DoD) $38 billion. While this is significantly lower than the $100-billion-plus price tag independent experts have calculated, CBO notes that its estimates were limited because “DoD did not respond to CBO’s requests for information.” Without help from the DoD, CBO could not include a number of known war costs in its analysis, including repairing damage to U.S. military bases in the region. items.title: Planbureau: doorsnee huishouden gaat er door Prinsjesdagplannen minder op achteruit
items.summary: De koopkracht ontwikkelt zich volgend jaar iets beter dan in augustus nog geraamd werd. Dat zegt het Centraal Planbureau. In augustus ging het CPB ervan uit dat een doorsnee huishouden er volgend jaar 0,3 procent op achteruitgaat in koopkracht. Door de maatregelen die op Prinsjesdag zijn aangekondigd is de raming nu een achteruitgang van 0,1 procent voor het doorsnee huishouden. Plusje voor laagste inkomens Alleen de laagste inkomens gaan er volgend jaar iets op vooruit: +0,2 procent. En gepensioneerden: +0,3 procent. Gepensioneerden krijgen er geld bij doordat pensioenfondsen er goed voorstaan en daardoor de pensioenen kunnen verhogen. De koopkracht van de laagste inkomens groeit een beetje doordat werkenden een grotere korting krijgen op hun inkomstenbelasting. "Er gebeurt wel iets om voor bepaalde groepen de koopkracht iets op te krikken", zegt CPB-directeur Pieter Hasekamp. "Het kabinet heeft ervoor gekozen om werkenden een steuntje in de rug te geven door die arbeidskorting iets te verhogen." clusters.headline: Planbureau ziet klimaatbeleid vastlopen: 'Enorme kloof tussen ambitie en beleid'

items.title: Planbureau ziet klimaatbeleid vastlopen: 'Enorme kloof tussen ambitie en beleid'
items.summary: De uitstoot van gassen die de aarde opwarmen daalt niet meer, klimaatdoelen zijn ver buiten bereik en ons land blijft voor energie nog jaren afhankelijk van gas, steenkool en olie uit het buitenland. Dat stelt het Planbureau voor de Leefomgeving (PBL) vast in een rapport over het klimaat- en energiebeleid dat jaarlijks verschijnt rond Prinsjesdag. Hoewel die conclusies niet erg anders zijn dan voorgaande jaren , klinken de onderzoekers steeds bezorgder. De aanpak van klimaatverandering zou vastlopen, en zonder nieuwe plannen gaat ons land de zichzelf gestelde doelen niet halen. Op deze koers mist ons land waarschijnlijk zijn streefdoel voor 2030. En komt niet in de buurt van de ambities voor de tientallen jaren erna. "We geven drie jaar op rij al aan dat de kans dat we het doel voor 2030 halen heel erg klein is", zegt Marko Hekkert, directeur van het PBL. "Dit jaar hebben we voor het eerst gekeken naar 2040. Wat je ziet is echt een enorme kloof tussen de ambitie aan de ene kant en het beleid aan de andere kant. Dat is nieuwe informatie waar het kabinet echt rekenschap van moet geven.

items.title: Austria says ‘lack of consensus’ at UN led to ban on Iran nuclear chief
items.summary: Austria says ‘lack of consensus’ at UN led to ban on Iran nuclear chief Austria said on Monday that a decision to exclude Iran’s nuclear chief, Mohammad Eslami, from entering the country to attend the annual meeting of the International Atomic Energy Agency in Vienna was because there was no consensus at the UN Security Council. Austria’s foreign ministry said it had requested an exemption to a current UN travel ban on Eslami but was denied. “Austria, as the host country of the International Atomic Energy Agency, applied to the relevant committee of the United Nations Security Council for an exemption from the existing UN travel ban for Mr Mohammed Eslami,” the ministry said. “Subsequently, Austria was informed by the president of the United Nations Security Council that the request had been rejected due to a lack of consensus. Entry could therefore not be permitted in view of Austria’s international obligations,” it added. “Austria wants to make negotiations in Vienna possible. We do so on the basis of international law and our international obligations.”

clusters.headline: European business survey – Bridging the gap between geopolitics and corporate strategy

items.title: European business survey – Bridging the gap between geopolitics and corporate strategy
items.summary: Geopolitical uncertainty has made economic security a central issue on the EU agenda. Companies are playing a crucial role in reducing strategic dependencies, strengthening resilience and diversifying supply chains. A pilot survey of 228 companies operating in Europe offers initial insights into how businesses assess geopolitical risks and what they expect from EU policymakers. The survey was conducted between November 2025 and January 2026 – several years into the Sino-US trade and tech conflict, the Ukrainian war, and supply chain concerns that emerged especially after the Covid-crisis but before recent escalations in transatlantic relations and the Iran conflict. Around 130–150 respondents answered the majority of the survey questions.

In the past four weeks, Americans have watched their government attempt to inflict an economic victory against Iran through Operation Economic Outcast, tightening a sanctions regime which for decades has strangled Iran’s economy without resolving the underlying dispute. Now, as that strategy flags, we have seen the Trump administration return to its older strategy of kinetic strikes against Iran. Those strikes, too, have failed to achieve their desired objectives. Facing the prospect of a self-inflicted defeat, the U.S. has now proposed two new paths forward. items.title: Iran says agreement with Oman would not mean the reopening of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran says agreement with Oman would not mean the reopening of Hormuz Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Sunday that Iran's anticipated agreement with Oman to govern the Strait of Hormuz will not trigger a reopening of the waterway. In comments to Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, Araghchi said Iran will provide details of the agreement and the new route maps to countries participating in a meeting with Gulf states in the Omani capital tomorrow, adding that the agreement does not “in any way” signal that the strait will reopen, which is conditional on the US honouring its commitments under the Memorandum of Understanding signed in Islamabad, he said. “Iran believes that the responsibility for ensuring security and stability in the region lies solely with the countries of the region,” Araghchi added.

Seven decades later, the UN is about to choose the successor to incumbent secretary-general Antonio Guterres , for what many regard as one of the trickiest roles on the world stage. Each term lasts five years, usually renewable for a second term. clusters.headline: Making Iraq ‘normal’ again: do mass arrests and cash seizures signal end to corruption?

items.title: Making Iraq ‘normal’ again: do mass arrests and cash seizures signal end to corruption?
items.summary: Government insiders say the new PM is unleashing an ‘earthquake’ to clean up the system. But Iraqis have heard it all before The gates of the Green Zone in Baghdad are made of five-metre-high armoured steel, reinforced with horizontal girders, and strung between concrete pillars and anti-blast walls. Police water cannon trucks are stationed nearby, along with armoured personnel carriers and squads of heavily armed soldiers. At the first sign of street protests – over failing electricity, unemployment or, more recently, the US-Israeli attacks on Iran – the gates are shut. X-shaped vehicle barriers, made from welded iron beams and mounted on wheels, sit ready at the roadside alongside coils of razor wire; both are slid across the street, sealing off the sprawling neighbourhood, home to the presidential palace, parliament, the prime minister’s office, the massive fortress-like US embassy, and other institutions, including the homes of scores of politicians and members of parliament. clusters.headline: Los hutíes, de las montañas de Yemen al control del mar Rojo

items.title: Los hutíes, de las montañas de Yemen al control del mar Rojo
items.summary: «Les golpeamos muy duro. Demostraron una enorme capacidad para soportar el castigo. Recibieron un castigo tremendo y se puede decir que hay mucha valentía ahí. Fue increíble lo que aguantaron», dijo Donald Trump en mayo de 2025 en la Casa Blanca al anunciar que Estados Unidos había llegado a un acuerdo con los hutíes para que estos dejaran de atacar barcos en el mar Rojo después de semanas de bombardeos contra ellos. clusters.headline: Brics backs Gaza ceasefire, calls for two-state solution for Palestine

items.title: Brics backs Gaza ceasefire, calls for two-state solution for Palestine
items.summary: Brics backs Gaza ceasefire, calls for two-state solution for Palestine Brics leaders on Saturday adopted a joint declaration calling for the extension of the “ceasefire” in Gaza and backing a two-state solution for Palestine. The declaration said root causes of conflicts must be tackled and reiterated the group's commitment to peaceful resolution through “dialogue, consultation and diplomacy”. The group, which comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, also raised concerns over the increasing nuclear risks and emphasised that nuclear safeguards, safety and security must be upheld, including in armed conflicts. The Brics leaders also praised the “ceasefire” in Lebanon and urged the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701, which calls for the cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah. The declaration also condemned unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort trade and violate World Trade Organisation rules.

Once líderes acudirán a la cita, con un mundo cada vez más convulso por contexto. items.title: Iran says four accused of plotting attack killed in Saravan
items.summary: Iran says four accused of plotting attack killed in Saravan Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its forces killed four people suspected of planning a "terrorist operation" in the Sistan-Baluchestan province. The IRGC said it targeted a “professional terrorist team” that was allegedly planning to attack the city of Saravan, in a statement published by the semi-official Tasnim news agency. The IRGC also said three Iranian soldiers were killed in the operation. There was no further detail in the statement about the fighting, which erupted after security forces allegedly raided a house used by what authorities called “mercenary terrorists”. The IRGC accused the United States and Israel of sowing “insecurity” in Sistan-Baluchestan.

clusters.headline: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'?

items.title: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'?
items.summary: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'? A quarter century is enough time to separate history from hysteria, consequences from intentions and reality from propaganda. On 11 September 2001, nearly 3,000 people were killed in horrific attacks that shocked the United States and the world. The attacks of 9/11 could have been treated as a grave crime requiring an international effort to identify, apprehend and prosecute those responsible. They could also have triggered a serious national debate about why such intense hostility towards the US had developed in many parts of the Muslim-majority world. Instead, the US's political establishment chose a radically different path. President George W Bush famously declared that the terrorists attacked the US because "they hate our freedoms". It was a convenient explanation because it absolved the American foreign policy establishment of any responsibility. items.title: De aanslagen in de VS hadden de zwaarste gevolgen in het Midden-Oosten
items.summary: In de Iraakse stad Falluja worden nog altijd baby's geboren met ernstige afwijkingen die het gevolg zijn van de oorlog die begon na aanslagen duizenden kilometers verderop. Amerikaanse troepen gebruikten tijdens de Irak-oorlog munitie met verarmd uranium. De gezondheidsproblemen, waaronder nierschade en vele vormen van kanker, behoren tot de vele tragische gevolgen van de aanslagen van 11 september 2001 die een kwart eeuw later nog nagalmen. Irak had niets met de aanslagen te maken. Toch werd het land een belangrijk strijdtoneel van de Amerikaanse War on Terror . Last week, Argentine President Javier Milei, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, announced a series of new measures aimed at pressuring Britain over the future of the islands. The most significant announcement was of new sanctions on companies involved in oil extraction in the waters around the Falklands, which Argentina has long claimed as its own. Argentina’s attempt to prevent the exploitation of the Falklands’ natural resources is a reminder that beneath the often farcical relitigating of sovereignty claims dating back to the 18th century is a very modern geopolitical conflict with real stakes for energy and maritime resources. After days of heavy fighting along a narrow plain known as the Tihama, on Thursday the Houthis routed Yemeni forces loyal to Saudi Arabia and seized the historic and strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha. items.summary: La respuesta de Irán a la guerra lanzada por Donald Trump y Benjamin Netanyahu tiene muchas formas y se extiende al mar Rojo. Los iraníes han convertido Ormuz en su arma más importante de presión y los hutíes, sus aliados yemeníes, se suman de lleno al conflicto con la captura del puerto de Moka, la entrada al estrecho de Bab El Mandeb (que se traduce del árabe como 'la puerta de las lágrimas'). Ormuz es la puerta energética del Golfo; Bab el Mandeb, la del mar Rojo y el Canal de Suez, una ruta clave del comercio entre Asia y Europa y punto de paso de alrededor del 7 por ciento del petróleo mundial. Y esto solo parece un primer paso, porque los hutíes avanzan para hacerse con el control total de la costa. La ofensiva de los rebeldes sorprendió a las fuerzas del Gobierno, que cuentan con el respaldo de Arabia Saudí, pero apenas ofrecieron resistencia lo que muestra su mala organización. En menos de una semana, los hutíes han tomado amplias partes del país y los bombardeos saudíes no han podido frenar a sus unidades terrestres, que avanzan en vehículos todoterreno y motocicletas. Business reporter Rob Davies explains his findings, including documents that raise questions about whether Puy du Fou’s activities tested the limits of EU sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2014 annexation of Crimea. items.title: Houthi's boeken grote terreinwinst in Jemen, nemen strategische havenstad in
items.summary: De Houthi's in Jemen hebben de havenstad Mokka ingenomen. Dat meldt persbureau Reuters, op basis van militaire bronnen van de Jemenitische regering. De inname van de stad markeert de grootste verschuiving van de frontlinies in vier jaar tijd. Vorige week begonnen de Houthi's, die worden gesteund door Iran, een offensief met vermoedelijk als doel om controle te krijgen over Bab el-Mandeb, de belangrijke zeestraat tussen Jemen en de Hoorn van Afrika. In de afgelopen dagen wonnen de Houthi's al flink terrein, met onder meer de herovering van de stad Hais, gisternacht. Niet ver daarvandaan ligt de stad Mokka. Vanochtend verschenen de eerste beelden vanuit de stad. Op beelden die de NOS verifieerde zijn onder meer Houthi-strijdkrachten te zien bij een verlaten voertuig van het Jemenitische staatsleger. Wie zijn de Houthi's? Dat en vier andere vragen leggen we in dit artikel aan je uit. Mokka is een strategisch gelegen havenstad aan de Rode Zee, iets ten noorden van de zeestraat. clusters.headline: Olivier Grondeau, ancien otage en Iran : «La poésie, c'est ce qui m'a fait tenir»

items.title: Olivier Grondeau, ancien otage en Iran : «La poésie, c'est ce qui m'a fait tenir»
items.summary: Olivier Grondeau a passé deux ans et demi en prison en Iran. Son nom est moins connu que ceux d’otages dont le cas a été médiatisé. Son histoire est assez proche. Arrêté à Chiraz le 12 octobre 2022, à l’époque des manifestations suivant la mort de Jina Mahsa Amini, il a été libéré en mars 2025. Il n’avait décidé de parler de sa situation que quelques mois plus tôt. Olivier Grondeau est un voyageur à tout petit budget, un poète, un grand lecteur, un ancien champion de scrabble. C’est son esprit, son humour, son imagination qui l’ont aidé à tenir. Il le raconte dans un livre publié chez l’iconoclaste : « Joseph dans la nuit »

items.title: Political Instability Meets Fiscal Limits: Is France the Euro’s Next Big Stress Test?
items.summary: With around half a year remaining before the next presidential election, France is in danger of becoming a stress test for the eurozone: a political crisis, a deteriorating fiscal position and growing market doubts about the country’s ability to finance its mounting debt burden are all converging. France faces a significant structural imbalance in its public finances. The budget deficit exceeds 5 per cent of GDP , while public expenditure stands at around 57 per cent of GDP. At the same time, public debt is rising steadily and could, without sufficient fiscal consolidation measures, exceed 130 per cent of GDP by 2030 . The interest burden on public debt is rising rapidly and could rise to more than 120 billion euros, equivalent to 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2030. The central challenge, however, may not lie in the fiscal arithmetic of the budget, but in the political capacity to address it. On the one hand, the costs of social welfare expenditure are no longer sustainable; on the other, the majority of the population continues to demand more state intervention. items.summary: While it is somewhat cliche to say that the “whole world changed” after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, it does not detract from the reality of the statement. In numerous tangible ways, the culture, security, and politics of the nation were never the same after al-Qaida hijackers in passenger planes left nearly 3,000 people dead in smoldering ruins across lower Manhattan, the Pentagon, and a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. For many of us who lived through it all, a quarter century has passed in a blink, while at the same time the pre-9/11 Washington era paradoxically seems so far away, and perhaps softened a bit by wistfulness and nostalgia. Conversely, the “post” era is pockmarked by wars, and an expansion of the national security state that was unimaginable a generation ago. Those born too early to witness the events of that day know nothing other than the current atmosphere of hyper-securitization and political polarization. It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say 9/11 and the “Global War on Terror” that followed are somewhere at the root of these woes. RS aske

items.title: By shunning the Taliban, the world is hurting normal Afghans
items.summary: Kabul — Last month, when Aisha Wahab of California became the first Afghan-American elected to Congress, her victory was heralded as a sign that Afghans had truly made their mark in American society. Afghan social media was inundated with messages of pride and celebration, Western-funded diaspora media outlets rushed out “who is Aisha Wahab” pieces, and even former President Hamid Karzai congratulated the 38-year-old on her victory. But that celebration was short-lived. items.summary: As diplomats prepare for the BRICS Summit in New Delhi this weekend, the Iran war is looming large. India, which assumed the BRICS chairmanship in January, was already facing the difficult responsibility of securing consensus to achieve concrete movement on a variety of trade, economic, and financial objectives. Now, the U.S.-Israeli campaign against Iran has dramatically complicated this effort, throwing the global economy into uncertainty and dividing BRICS countries, including some that are actively participating on either side of the conflict. The tensions within the bloc are far more significant than they were leading into last year’s summit in Brazil, which took place shortly after the 12-Day War against Iran. But it was not clear whether his campaign-style speech would appeal to the critical swing voters who opinion polls show have drifted away from Trump's party, amid growing dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the war on Iran. items.summary: Oil prices breach $100 as Iran-US attacks escalate Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel on Wednesday to settle at their highest close since late May after Iran and the US struck tankers in the biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began. Front-month Brent crude futures settled up $3.29, or 3.4%, at $101.21 a barrel, after touching a high of $101.58. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was up $3.02, or 3.25%, at $96.05 a barrel. Both benchmarks closed at their highest since May 22. Since late May, oil benchmarks have generally traded well below the $100-per-barrel psychological threshold, reflecting expectations that the conflict would remain on a low simmer. Report by Reuters

clusters.headline: How Congress gave up its power over war and peace

items.title: How Congress gave up its power over war and peace
items.summary: In 1973, after it was discovered that the U.S. had secretly bombed Cambodia, Congress took action. In an effort to assert its power over matters of war and peace, Congress pushed through the War Powers Resolution despite then-President Richard Nixon’s veto, and it has been law ever since. Unfortunately, congressional enforcement of the War Powers Resolution has been mixed. In 2026 alone, Congress has put forward some 19 war powers resolutions in an attempt to rein in hostilities in Iran, Venezuela, Cuba, and Lebanon. So far, none of these resolutions has stopped a conflict. Take Iran, for example. There have been eight votes to end the war, seven of which failed. Just one of these passed and only because Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) changed course after losing his primary to a challenger endorsed by President Donald Trump, giving him leeway to vote against the bulk of the Republican Party. Cassidy’s move highlights one of the main problems with the War Powers Resolution: too many of our elected officials cast votes for political gain, not American interests. items.title: Dodental na luchtaanval op Houthi-gevangenis in Jemen loopt op tot 23
items.summary: Bij een luchtaanval op een gevangenis in het noorden van Jemen zijn zeker 23 mensen om het leven gekomen. Reddingswerkers hebben vandaag vier lichamen geborgen uit het puin van de gevangenis, die maandag instortte na een aanval van de door Saudi-Arabië geleide coalitie. De gevangenis stond in de strategisch gelegen stad Hazm, in de provincie Jawf. Volgens de Houthi's wordt nog gezocht naar zeven vermisten. Bij de aanval raakten zeker zeven mensen gewond. Onder hen was een vrouw die haar echtgenoot in de gevangenis bezocht. De identiteit van de dodelijke slachtoffers is nog niet vastgesteld. De aanval maakt deel uit van een nieuwe escalatie van het conflict in Jemen. De door Saudi-Arabië geleide coalitie voerde vanochtend nieuwe luchtaanvallen uit op militaire doelen van de Houthi's in de provincies Marib en Jawf. De Houthi's reageerden eerder met een reeks raket- en droneaanvallen op het zuiden van Saudi-Arabië. Daarbij raakten volgens de autoriteiten 73 mensen gewond. During the call, Dar emphasised the critical need for secure shipping routes and uninterrupted energy supplies, warning of the potential fallout for developing nations and global supply chains. Macron said the meeting would focus on coordinating strategic stockpile levels, cooperation on exports and production capacity, and possible releases of strategic reserves. Macron said that the aim of the meeting was to strengthen cooperation and avoid unnecessary tensions between G7 countries and their key partners. He said France had initiated an international defence mission with the International Maritime Organization last April aimed at escorting tankers and container ships through the strategic waterway once an agreement was reached. Macron said reopening Hormuz depended on a deal between Iran and the United States, which he said appeared unlikely in the short term. items.summary: Turkey revokes licence of Iran's Bank Mellat as US sanctions intensify Turkey has revoked the operating licence of Iran’s Bank Mellat, which remains on the US Treasury’s sanctions list, as Washington intensifies economic pressure on Tehran. Turkey’s Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency’s decision to revoke  the bank’s main Istanbul branch’s licence after 44 years did not directly link the move to US sanctions, Al Jazeera reported. The agency cited a provision allowing a licence to be withdrawn if continued operations pose a risk to depositors’ rights or the stability of the financial system. Washington designated the bank in 2018, accusing it of providing financial support to Mehr Eqtesad Bank, which the US links to Iran’s Basij.

items.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted Houthi drone near Mecca
items.summary: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted Houthi drone near Mecca Saudi Arabia's air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, said a spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis. The security of Islam's two holiest sites and of pilgrims was a "red line", coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said early on Wednesday, adding that the coalition would take necessary deterrent measures against the Houthis. Mecca, home to shrines sacred to Muslims worldwide, is Islam's holiest city and the focal point of the annual hajj pilgrimage, one of the five pillars of Islam, which millions of Muslims undertake each year. Malki described the incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca, following what the coalition said was a ballistic missile launch in July 2017. items.title: Trump's govt makes 'treasonous' claim of weapons shortages
items.summary: In the last two days, a pair of government reports confirmed what many outside analysts have claimed: the Iran war has been extraordinarily costly for the U.S. military and for the American public. A Congressional Budget Office (CBO) analysis released Tuesday afternoon found that the Iran war has already cost the Department of Defense (DoD) $38 billion. While this is significantly lower than the $100-billion-plus price tag independent experts have calculated, CBO notes that its estimates were limited because “DoD did not respond to CBO’s requests for information.” Without help from the DoD, CBO could not include a number of known war costs in its analysis, including repairing damage to U.S. military bases in the region. Those costs alone could top $200 billion , according to experts. What CBO could confirm was that the war has been a disaster for the U.S. economy and military readiness. The CBO analysis estimates that the inflation rate is now expected to be a full half-point higher in 2027 than it was before the war began, almost entirely because of higher global energy costs result

items.title: Massie tells RS why he went after Hegseth and not Trump
items.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) tells Responsible Statecraft that he is initiating eight articles of impeachment against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth because Congress has “exhausted every other remedy to make things right.” After a speech on the floor Tuesday, Massie said is forcing a vote on the articles in the House, which would likely happen on Thursday before the chamber recesses for the midterms. The resolution is quite a brief against Hegseth, covering U.S. military actions in Iran, Yemen, and Venezuela, as well as accusing Hegseth of minimizing civilian deaths and abridging freedom of speech. Impeachment votes are privileged in the House, which means the measure can bypass the rules and go straight to a floor vote after debate. The articles would have to get a motion, however, which would require a majority vote. It is not clear how many Democrats would vote for it. Democrats just killed a resolution to impeach President Donald Trump by one of their own , Rep. Al Green (D-Texas). We spoke to Massie on Tuesday. items.title: Iran war cost US $38bn and significantly depleted missile stockpile, report finds
items.summary: Damaging budget report estimates cost would grow $3bn per month and stockpile could take five years to rebuild The war in Iran has cost the US at least $38bn and left its stockpile of defensive missiles so depleted it could take five years to rebuild, the non-partisan Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has found, in a damaging report less than two months before midterm elections where the war and the cost of living crisis will likely hurt Republicans at the polls. The economic report comes one day after the Pentagon’s inspector general finally released its own first review of the war, saying that the US spent $22.3bn on munitions alone through 30 June, put total spending at $33.4bn and found the fighting had “resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply”. items.title: Iran war cost hits $38bn, forecast to rise $3bn a month, CBO says
items.summary: Iran war cost hits $38bn, forecast to rise $3bn a month, CBO says The six-month-old US war on Iran has cost $38bn so far, and that amount is projected to rise by $3bn a month, Congress's nonpartisan bookkeeper reported on Tuesday, as the Trump administration searches for ways to end the war and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz. The war is expected to increase inflation by 0.5 percent in the first three months of 2027, according to the Congressional Budget Office accounting, which totalled expenses through 1 August. The mounting costs have strained US munitions stockpiles and driven up energy prices, adding pressure on an already stretched federal budget.

items.title: Iraq eyes Europe as it seeks to diversify oil exports
items.summary: Iraq eyes Europe as it seeks to diversify oil exports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said on Tuesday that he discussed selling oil to Europe during visits to France and Germany, as Baghdad seeks to diversify its export routes and reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz. During a press conference with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, Zaidi said "we want to expand and diversify our export routes". He added that "Iraq cannot remain hostage to a single corridor" as recent events have demonstrated, referring to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blockaded by Iran during the war. Zaidi said that he had discussed oil exports to Europe with Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron, whom he met in Paris on Monday.

items.title: AIVD: Iran breekt online in bij dissidenten om gevoelige informatie te stelen
items.summary: Iran gebruikt spionagesoftware om gevoelige informatie te verzamelen over kritische Iraniërs die in het Westen wonen. Daarvoor waarschuwt de Nederlandse inlichtingendienst AIVD, samen met de Amerikaanse FBI en het Britse cybersecuritycentrum NCSC. Iraanse diensten proberen via sociale media contact te leggen met dissidenten, activisten en journalisten en hun vertrouwen te winnen. Daarna vragen de Iraanse "cyberactoren" hen om een bestand te downloaden en dat te openen, zeggen de diensten. 'Volledige controle' Zodra het bestand is geopend heeft de software, Chosen Brick, volgens de AIVD "volledige controle over het apparaat". Zo kan het Iraanse regime toegang krijgen tot contactpersonen, e-mails en socialemedia-accounts van het slachtoffer. Ook kan de software beveiligingsinstellingen aanpassen of die in- of uitschakelen en schermafbeeldingen maken. Vooral apparaten van Windows zouden het doelwit zijn. items.title: Planbureau: doorsnee huishouden gaat er door Prinsjesdagplannen minder op achteruit
items.summary: De koopkracht ontwikkelt zich volgend jaar iets beter dan in augustus nog geraamd werd. Dat zegt het Centraal Planbureau. In augustus ging het CPB ervan uit dat een doorsnee huishouden er volgend jaar 0,3 procent op achteruitgaat in koopkracht. Door de maatregelen die op Prinsjesdag zijn aangekondigd is de raming nu een achteruitgang van 0,1 procent voor het doorsnee huishouden. Plusje voor laagste inkomens Alleen de laagste inkomens gaan er volgend jaar iets op vooruit: +0,2 procent. En gepensioneerden: +0,3 procent. items.title: Houthi attacks expose gaps in Pakistan's defence pact with Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Houthi attacks expose gaps in Pakistan's defence pact with Saudi Arabia After positioning itself as a regional mediator by facilitating talks between Washington and Tehran, Pakistan marked a major milestone in its expanding diplomacy last month: the signing of a trilateral defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in Islam’s holiest city. Signed in Mecca on 7 August, the Joint Defence Agreement states that an attack on one signatory will be treated as an attack on all, drawing immediate comparisons to Nato’s Article 5, even as analysts cautioned against taking the clause too literally. That commitment was quickly tested on 8 September, when Iran-backed Houthi forces launched a massive drone and missile barrage into Saudi Arabia, striking critical military and energy infrastructure. Overnight, an abstract commitment turned into a high-stakes operational question. Neither Islamabad nor Ankara launched military counter-operations alongside Riyadh, choosing firm diplomatic statements instead. Saudi-Arabië gebruikt de 1200 kilometer lange East-West Pipeline, die dwars door het land loopt, om ruwe olie van havens aan de Perzische Golf naar havens aan de westkust, aan de Rode Zee, te transporteren. Van daaruit kan de olie op tankers worden geladen voor export. Via de pijpleiding kan Saudi-Arabië de Straat van Hormuz omzeilen bij de export van olie. In die belangrijke zeestraat is het al tijden onrustig en is het scheepvaartverkeer bijna volledig stilgevallen . Onrust in Jemen Een van de functionarissen zegt dat de leiding mogelijk nog gedeeltelijk in gebruik kan blijven tijdens de herstelwerkzaamheden. De pijpleiding heeft een capaciteit van maximaal 7 miljoen vaten olie per dag. Volgens Saudi-Arabië zitten door Iran gesteunde milities in Irak achter de aanval. items.title: Planbureau ziet klimaatbeleid vastlopen: 'Enorme kloof tussen ambitie en beleid'
items.summary: De uitstoot van gassen die de aarde opwarmen daalt niet meer, klimaatdoelen zijn ver buiten bereik en ons land blijft voor energie nog jaren afhankelijk van gas, steenkool en olie uit het buitenland. Dat stelt het Planbureau voor de Leefomgeving (PBL) vast in een rapport over het klimaat- en energiebeleid dat jaarlijks verschijnt rond Prinsjesdag. Hoewel die conclusies niet erg anders zijn dan voorgaande jaren , klinken de onderzoekers steeds bezorgder. De aanpak van klimaatverandering zou vastlopen, en zonder nieuwe plannen gaat ons land de zichzelf gestelde doelen niet halen. Op deze koers mist ons land waarschijnlijk zijn streefdoel voor 2030. En komt niet in de buurt van de ambities voor de tientallen jaren erna. "We geven drie jaar op rij al aan dat de kans dat we het doel voor 2030 halen heel erg klein is", zegt Marko Hekkert, directeur van het PBL. "Dit jaar hebben we voor het eerst gekeken naar 2040. Wat je ziet is echt een enorme kloof tussen de ambitie aan de ene kant en het beleid aan de andere kant. Dat is nieuwe informatie waar het kabinet echt rekenschap van moet geven.

items.title: Austria says ‘lack of consensus’ at UN led to ban on Iran nuclear chief
items.summary: Austria says ‘lack of consensus’ at UN led to ban on Iran nuclear chief Austria said on Monday that a decision to exclude Iran’s nuclear chief, Mohammad Eslami, from entering the country to attend the annual meeting of the International Atomic Energy Agency in Vienna was because there was no consensus at the UN Security Council. Austria’s foreign ministry said it had requested an exemption to a current UN travel ban on Eslami but was denied. “Austria, as the host country of the International Atomic Energy Agency, applied to the relevant committee of the United Nations Security Council for an exemption from the existing UN travel ban for Mr Mohammed Eslami,” the ministry said. “Subsequently, Austria was informed by the president of the United Nations Security Council that the request had been rejected due to a lack of consensus. Entry could therefore not be permitted in view of Austria’s international obligations,” it added. “Austria wants to make negotiations in Vienna possible. We do so on the basis of international law and our international obligations.”

items.title: European business survey – Bridging the gap between geopolitics and corporate strategy
items.summary: Geopolitical uncertainty has made economic security a central issue on the EU agenda. Companies are playing a crucial role in reducing strategic dependencies, strengthening resilience and diversifying supply chains. A pilot survey of 228 companies operating in Europe offers initial insights into how businesses assess geopolitical risks and what they expect from EU policymakers. The survey was conducted between November 2025 and January 2026 – several years into the Sino-US trade and tech conflict, the Ukrainian war, and supply chain concerns that emerged especially after the Covid-crisis but before recent escalations in transatlantic relations and the Iran conflict. Around 130–150 respondents answered the majority of the survey questions.

items.title: US opposes Iran nuclear chief attending IAEA conference
items.summary: US opposes Iran nuclear chief attending IAEA conference The United States opposed the head of Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation attending the annual conference of the UN nuclear watchdog, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Monday. Speaking to reporters in Vienna, where the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is based, Wright said Mohammad Eslami was subject to US sanctions and had been denied a request for a waiver. “He’s a sanctioned individual and we don’t want sanctioned individuals evading their sanctions. He asked for a waiver of the sanctions and it was denied,” Wright said. Eslami has regularly attended and addressed the IAEA General Conference since becoming head of Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation in 2021. Iranian state television said Eslami and a delegation travelled to Vienna on a regular flight Saturday but were “blocked on the way because of obstructions by the United States”.

items.title: Iran blacklists 77 ships accused of breaking Strait of Hormuz rules
items.summary: Iran blacklists 77 ships accused of breaking Strait of Hormuz rules Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority has placed 77 vessels on a list of ships it accuses of “violating Iranian protocols for the Strait of Hormuz”. The Iranian body, which oversees transit requests through the waterway, said the vessels could face “fines, detention or confiscation” if they attempt future crossings. It warned that it would also list commercial ships that cooperate with the US and its allies. Tehran disputes repeated assertions by US President Donald Trump that the American military exercises “total control” over the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says it will not reopen the strait until Washington meets its demands over US attacks, reparations and sanctions.

items.title: How Trump's Iran operation turned into a forever war
items.summary: As the United States has struggled to secure its four primary objectives in the Iran War — achieving regime change, dismantling long-range ballistic missiles, eliminating nuclear enrichment, and halting Tehran’s support for regional proxies — U.S. officials have rolled out a series of tried-and-failed theories for how to achieve those goals. In the past four weeks, Americans have watched their government attempt to inflict an economic victory against Iran through Operation Economic Outcast, tightening a sanctions regime which for decades has strangled Iran’s economy without resolving the underlying dispute. Now, as that strategy flags, we have seen the Trump administration return to its older strategy of kinetic strikes against Iran. Those strikes, too, have failed to achieve their desired objectives. Facing the prospect of a self-inflicted defeat, the U.S. has now proposed two new paths forward. items.summary: Oil prices rise sharply as Middle East escalation risks disruption to supplies Oil prices rose sharply on Monday, pushing Brent crude above $107 a barrel as escalating tensions in the Middle East stoked fears of disruptions to global energy supplies. Brent crude for November delivery gained 2.8 percent to $107.54 a barrel, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate for October rose 2.3 percent to $102.34. Both contracts extended last week's gains after climbing back above the $100 threshold. Global oil supplies face a challenge after Saudi Arabia shut an oil pipeline following a drone attack and Iran-backed Houthis took control of a key island overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait,  a chokepoint for Red Sea maritime traffic.

items.title: Saudi Arabian pipeline outage threatens global oil supply
items.summary: Saudi Arabian pipeline outage threatens global oil supply Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4 percent of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders told Reuters on Sunday. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs since the start of the US-Iran war. Following the drone attacks launched from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to shut its huge East-West oil pipeline on Friday, Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay offline. Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing.

items.title: Making Iraq ‘normal’ again: do mass arrests and cash seizures signal end to corruption?
items.summary: Government insiders say the new PM is unleashing an ‘earthquake’ to clean up the system. But Iraqis have heard it all before The gates of the Green Zone in Baghdad are made of five-metre-high armoured steel, reinforced with horizontal girders, and strung between concrete pillars and anti-blast walls. Police water cannon trucks are stationed nearby, along with armoured personnel carriers and squads of heavily armed soldiers. At the first sign of street protests – over failing electricity, unemployment or, more recently, the US-Israeli attacks on Iran – the gates are shut. X-shaped vehicle barriers, made from welded iron beams and mounted on wheels, sit ready at the roadside alongside coils of razor wire; both are slid across the street, sealing off the sprawling neighbourhood, home to the presidential palace, parliament, the prime minister’s office, the massive fortress-like US embassy, and other institutions, including the homes of scores of politicians and members of parliament. Houthi official Abdelkader al-Murtada said they were prisoners of war who had spent up to eight years in jail before the Iran-backed group launched a rapid offensive to take over areas bordering the Bab al-Mandab Strait. "We have welcomed 210 of our prisoners, freed from Saudi enemy prisons on the west coast," Murtada said at a conference in the capital Sanaa. Fighters loyal to the Houthi authorities march during a rally to recruit more fighters, in Sanaa, Yemen, on 10 September 2026 (Mohammed Huwais/AFP) The Houthis had already controlled large parts of northern Yemen, including most of the country's populated areas and the major cities of Sanaa and Hodeida, before making dramatic advances last week.

items.title: Brics backs Gaza ceasefire, calls for two-state solution for Palestine
items.summary: Brics backs Gaza ceasefire, calls for two-state solution for Palestine Brics leaders on Saturday adopted a joint declaration calling for the extension of the “ceasefire” in Gaza and backing a two-state solution for Palestine. The declaration said root causes of conflicts must be tackled and reiterated the group's commitment to peaceful resolution through “dialogue, consultation and diplomacy”. The group, which comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, also raised concerns over the increasing nuclear risks and emphasised that nuclear safeguards, safety and security must be upheld, including in armed conflicts. The Brics leaders also praised the “ceasefire” in Lebanon and urged the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701, which calls for the cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah. The declaration also condemned unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort trade and violate World Trade Organisation rules.

items.summary: Si caben dudas respecto a la existencia misma del llamado Sur Global –esa locución que pretende aunar a los países no desarrollados en un bloque geopolítico–, no digamos ya respecto a quién lo lidera. Los dos mandatarios con pretensiones de hacerlo, el líder chino Xi Jinping y el primer ministro indio Narendra Modi , mantienen este fin de semana un encuentro para comprobar hasta qué punto resultan compatibles sus respectivas visiones de la relación bilateral y el mundo en general.Xi realiza su primer viaje a India en siete años con motivo de la celebración de la cumbre de los BRICS, otro acrónimo elevado a categoría difusa. Este organismo, concebido como contrapeso a Occidente , no cuenta con la fuerza de un propósito común pero sí con la de los números, pues aglutina a la mitad de la población terrestre, dos quintos del PIB global y un cuarto del comercio internacional . Once líderes acudirán a la cita, con un mundo cada vez más convulso por contexto. items.title: Will Houthis' rapid advance drag US, Saudi Arabia back into Yemen?
items.summary: This week, after launching an unprecedented series of strikes on Saudi Arabia, the Houthis embarked on a sweeping offensive in Yemen, seizing large swathes of territory along the Red Sea coast. These rapid changes have pushed Yemen’s war back into the regional arena, threatening Red Sea shipping and placing the country’s Saudi-backed, internationally-recognized government on the back foot. The rapid reversal came only days after the government declared a campaign to retake Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, amid a broader escalation in fighting across the country. A 2022 truce had reduced large-scale combat and allowed Saudi Arabia to distance itself from the conflict, but it left the capital under Houthi control and did nothing to establish centralized control over the country and its heavy weapons. Now, as the Houthis advance rapidly toward government strongholds in the south, Yemen’s military is scrambling to regroup and make progress on its planned offensive in the north. items.title: Iran used Chinese satellite images for attack on US base in Jordan
items.summary: Iran used Chinese satellite images for attack on US base in Jordan Iran used Chinese satellite images to carry out its attack on an American base in Jordan that killed three US troops in July, The Wall Street Journal reported. Citing US officials familiar with details of the incident, the newspaper reported that Tehran had acquired high-resolution satellite images of Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, which suffered extensive damage in the strike. The newspaper reported that US officials declined to identify the Chinese entities that supplied the imagery to Iran and did not allege direct involvement by Beijing.

items.title: Iranian media: Houthis take control of Strait of Mandeb after seizing Mayyun Island
items.summary: Iranian media: Houthis take control of Strait of Mandeb after seizing Mayyun Island Yemen’s Houthis control the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait after seizing Mayyun Island, also known as Perim Island, Iran’s Tasnim News Agency reported. Located at the centre of the Bab al-Mandab Strait,  Mayyun Island is a key monitoring point overlooking the vital maritime passage. Two Yemeni sources also told Reuters that Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces had withdrawn from Perim Island. The development came after Houthis seized the western coastal city of Mocha, forcing the government forces to retreat toward the south and the city of Dhubab. The Sanaa-based Yemen Press Agency, citing field sources, said Houthi forces seized the al-Omari camp overlooking the strait. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree was also reported as saying that navigation in the Red Sea was safe except for Saudi ships, suggesting the group now has control over the Strait of Mandeb. Twee Amerikaanse functionarissen zeggen tegen CNN dat er brand is ontstaan bij twee pompstations. Hoelang het gaat duren om de schade te herstellen, is niet bekend. Bij de aanvallen zouden ook meerdere mensen gewond zijn geraakt. Zij hebben volgens de Saudische autoriteiten medische hulp gekregen. He did not mention the war in Iran directly, and he only brought up foreign policy as an example of an issue that divides the party’s base. He urged voters not to “throw the baby out with the bathwater” because “you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here or there.” The acknowledgement of foreign policy as a divisive issue in the MAGA coalition is a stark retreat for Vance, who staked his 2023 endorsement of Trump on the fact that “he started no wars despite enormous pressure from his own party and even members of his own administration,” framing the president’s America First record as a much-needed deviation from decades of bipartisan hawkishness. A few wars later, Vance appears to have backed down from the anti-war aspects of the America First movement. items.summary: UN says Yemen’s Houthis seized humanitarian facility in Mocha A senior United Nations spokesperson says that Yemen’s Houthis seized a humanitarian facility in Mocha, Al Jazeera reported, citing Farhan Haq, deputy spokesperson for the secretary-general, as saying. Haq said in a news briefing on Friday that the site housed staff from UN agencies, but all personnel were safe and had already departed. No UN employees remain in Mocha, Haq added, after eight Yemeni staff members who were in the area relocated from Mocha to nearby Aden, Turbah and Taiz before the Iran-allied group’s swift battlefield advance. “Humanitarian personnel, premises and assets must be respected and protected at all times,” he said.

items.title: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'?
items.summary: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'? A quarter century is enough time to separate history from hysteria, consequences from intentions and reality from propaganda. On 11 September 2001, nearly 3,000 people were killed in horrific attacks that shocked the United States and the world. The attacks of 9/11 could have been treated as a grave crime requiring an international effort to identify, apprehend and prosecute those responsible. They could also have triggered a serious national debate about why such intense hostility towards the US had developed in many parts of the Muslim-majority world. Instead, the US's political establishment chose a radically different path. President George W Bush famously declared that the terrorists attacked the US because "they hate our freedoms". It was a convenient explanation because it absolved the American foreign policy establishment of any responsibility. items.summary: Satellite images show smoke near Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline Satellite images showed smoke rising near Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, one of the kingdom’s key energy assets, Reuters has reported. The news agency said Saudi authorities did not immediately report any incident at the site. The East-West Pipeline has become increasingly important for Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, enabling state oil giant Aramco to ship crude from the kingdom’s eastern coast to the Red Sea on its western coast. It offers an alternative route for sending crude through the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic global energy chokepoint. items.summary: Iran president says he does not favour continuing the war Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he does not support continuing the war, but he stressed that Iran needs to improve its resistance to future challenges so that it does not have to negotiate from a position of weakness. Speaking to heads of the country’s leading universities, Pezeshkian said universities should support the government across areas including the economy, management, culture and literature, ISNA reported. Pezeshkian also called for greater involvement of students in tackling national issues. “We must make sure that instead of engaging in protest, they engage in solving problems,” he said. The president said he had “no political angle with anyone”, adding, “Whoever helps us solve the country’s problems, with whatever political viewpoint, I accept.” “Economic measures must take into account the country’s conditions, otherwise they will lead to negative results and losses instead of addressing the issues,” Pezeshkian said.

items.title: Trump’s clash with Canada is his latest imperialistic embarrassment | Sidney Blumenthal
items.summary: The president’s chaotic schemes of aggrandizement, from Venezuela to Iran, have no larger rationale Trumpism is the lowest stage of imperialism. “We’re not going to invade Greenland. We’re going to buy it,” Donald Trump reportedly told the annual black-tie dinner on 1 February of the private Alfalfa Club, an assemblage of prominent Washington figures, a number of whom he had publicly humiliated, and others he was investigating or suing. “It’s never been my intention to make Greenland the 51st state. The newspaper said that Vance, who opposed the war from the outset, sought direct intel from commander on “objectives, tactics, casualty estimates, what the Iranians would do in the Strait of Hormuz, how adaptable they had become and how much punishment their government could absorb”. Vance wanted the commanders’ “individual judgments, in their own words, before they were consolidated into a Pentagon view”, the report said. He also asked for a detailed accounting of what remained in the commanders’ stockpiles, and how the transfer of weapons to the Middle East would affect their ability to deter China, Russia and North Korea. On the stockpiles, the commanders “were blunt”, NYT reported, adding, “they were most worried about their depleted stocks of Patriot interceptors, the backbone of their air defences”. items.title: Iranian strikes damaged multiple aircraft at Jordan base, report says
items.summary: Iranian strikes damaged multiple aircraft at Jordan base, report says Iranian strikes damaged multiple American military aircraft this week on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, a US official told Reuters. The US military, the highest-funded in the world, suffered material damage even before Iran's strikes on Tuesday. This includes the destruction of more than two dozen drones, Iran striking fighter jets, and aircraft being lost to accidents. According to a May report from the Congressional Research Service, 42 US military aircraft had already been lost or damaged in the conflict. Since the Iran war started in February, 18 US service members have been killed and over 800 injured. A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said Iran's attack hit one A-10 Thunderbolt II, known as the Warthog, leaving it with a missing wing, while roughly eight F-15s sustained light damage and were returned to service. Iran's strike on the US base in Jordan came after US forces said they destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers. Report by Reuters

items.title: US diesel prices surpass $6 a gallon for first time as oil hits highest since May
items.summary: US diesel prices surpass $6 a gallon for first time as oil hits highest since May The US national average price of diesel on Thursday surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time ever, according to price tracker GasBuddy, as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russia’s refineries have squeezed supply. The latest surge in fuel costs is adding to inflationary pressures that have already strained consumers and businesses this year, creating a political headache for President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers as they seek to defend thin congressional majorities in November's midterm elections. Crude oil futures on Thursday hit their highest level since mid-May. Brent settled at $107.63 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate futures at $102.48 a barrel.

IRGC added that the sea drone had been used in the region by the US Fifth Fleet stationed in Bahrain. Washington has previously used Saildrone Explorer USs to gather data and images in the Gulf. Iran told the Houthis last week to escalate their attacks on Saudi Arabia, a close US ally, and promised more funding, weapons and senior officers to help them do so, two Iranian sources said. Several senior Revolutionary Guards commanders had already travelled to Yemen to oversee and command Houthi attacks directed against Saudi Arabia after weeks of discussions over military strategy, a regional diplomat briefed by Tehran said. A third Iranian source, an official, said Iran had held several meetings with allies including the Houthis and that the move on Mocha was a Houthi rather than Iranian decision. However, it had helped Iran by putting upward pressure on oil prices and hurting the United States and Saudi Arabia, the official added. Reporting by Reuters

items.summary: Olivier Grondeau a passé deux ans et demi en prison en Iran. Son nom est moins connu que ceux d’otages dont le cas a été médiatisé. Son histoire est assez proche. Arrêté à Chiraz le 12 octobre 2022, à l’époque des manifestations suivant la mort de Jina Mahsa Amini, il a été libéré en mars 2025. Il n’avait décidé de parler de sa situation que quelques mois plus tôt. Olivier Grondeau est un voyageur à tout petit budget, un poète, un grand lecteur, un ancien champion de scrabble. C’est son esprit, son humour, son imagination qui l’ont aidé à tenir. Il le raconte dans un livre publié chez l’iconoclaste : « Joseph dans la nuit »

items.title: Political Instability Meets Fiscal Limits: Is France the Euro’s Next Big Stress Test?
items.summary: With around half a year remaining before the next presidential election, France is in danger of becoming a stress test for the eurozone: a political crisis, a deteriorating fiscal position and growing market doubts about the country’s ability to finance its mounting debt burden are all converging. France faces a significant structural imbalance in its public finances. The budget deficit exceeds 5 per cent of GDP , while public expenditure stands at around 57 per cent of GDP. At the same time, public debt is rising steadily and could, without sufficient fiscal consolidation measures, exceed 130 per cent of GDP by 2030 . The interest burden on public debt is rising rapidly and could rise to more than 120 billion euros, equivalent to 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2030. The central challenge, however, may not lie in the fiscal arithmetic of the budget, but in the political capacity to address it. items.summary: Underwater drone capture gives Tehran opportunity to reverse engineer vessel Iran's capture of a US military underwater drone gives Tehran an opportunity to study and potentially reverse engineer the vessel, delivering a setback for the Pentagon and drone maker Anduril. The US military and Anduril have downplayed the significance of the drone falling into Iranian hands. The vessel, a Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle designed for long-range surveillance and other undersea missions, is among a new generation of military drones intended to operate for days with little human intervention. Washington has previously treated the loss of advanced drones to Iran as a serious matter. After Iran captured an RQ-170 Sentinel stealth reconnaissance drone in 2011, then-President Barack Obama publicly asked Tehran to return the aircraft. Iran later claimed it had reverse-engineered the drone and subsequently unveiled domestically produced models that appeared to draw heavily on its design. Symposium: What I miss most about pre-9/11 America
items.summary: While it is somewhat cliche to say that the “whole world changed” after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, it does not detract from the reality of the statement. In numerous tangible ways, the culture, security, and politics of the nation were never the same after al-Qaida hijackers in passenger planes left nearly 3,000 people dead in smoldering ruins across lower Manhattan, the Pentagon, and a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. For many of us who lived through it all, a quarter century has passed in a blink, while at the same time the pre-9/11 Washington era paradoxically seems so far away, and perhaps softened a bit by wistfulness and nostalgia. Conversely, the “post” era is pockmarked by wars, and an expansion of the national security state that was unimaginable a generation ago. Those born too early to witness the events of that day know nothing other than the current atmosphere of hyper-securitization and political polarization. items.title: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports
items.summary: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports Top White House advisers, including vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio, have privately warned president Donald Trump that the conflict with Iran could extend through the remainder of his presidency, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials. The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The advisers told Trump in private discussions in the Oval Office and the Situation Room that Tehran could continue to resist US pressure, potentially prolonging the conflict beyond Inauguration Day in January 2029, the Journal added. The reported warning contrasts with Trump's own public remarks about the war. The president said on Wednesday he expected the war to end "immediately after" the US midterm elections in November, arguing that Iran was trying to influence the vote but would be unable to sustain its resistance much longer. Trump also acknowledged diplomatic talks are still a possibility but were not preferred. Report by Reuters

items.title: How Congress gave up its power over war and peace
items.summary: In 1973, after it was discovered that the U.S. had secretly bombed Cambodia, Congress took action. In an effort to assert its power over matters of war and peace, Congress pushed through the War Powers Resolution despite then-President Richard Nixon’s veto, and it has been law ever since. Unfortunately, congressional enforcement of the War Powers Resolution has been mixed. In 2026 alone, Congress has put forward some 19 war powers resolutions in an attempt to rein in hostilities in Iran, Venezuela, Cuba, and Lebanon. So far, none of these resolutions has stopped a conflict. Take Iran, for example. There have been eight votes to end the war, seven of which failed. Just one of these passed and only because Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) changed course after losing his primary to a challenger endorsed by President Donald Trump, giving him leeway to vote against the bulk of the Republican Party. Cassidy’s move highlights one of the main problems with the War Powers Resolution: too many of our elected officials cast votes for political gain, not American interests. items.summary: Bij een luchtaanval op een gevangenis in het noorden van Jemen zijn zeker 23 mensen om het leven gekomen. Reddingswerkers hebben vandaag vier lichamen geborgen uit het puin van de gevangenis, die maandag instortte na een aanval van de door Saudi-Arabië geleide coalitie. De gevangenis stond in de strategisch gelegen stad Hazm, in de provincie Jawf. Volgens de Houthi's wordt nog gezocht naar zeven vermisten. Bij de aanval raakten zeker zeven mensen gewond. Onder hen was een vrouw die haar echtgenoot in de gevangenis bezocht. De identiteit van de dodelijke slachtoffers is nog niet vastgesteld. De aanval maakt deel uit van een nieuwe escalatie van het conflict in Jemen. De door Saudi-Arabië geleide coalitie voerde vanochtend nieuwe luchtaanvallen uit op militaire doelen van de Houthi's in de provincies Marib en Jawf.
